mbm-2401.clue: My first belt is one notch optimistic.
mbm-2401.quote: I punched the holes on my first leather belt with the marks upside down. The last hole has a small sun stamped round it. I save that one for pie night.

mbm-2402.clue: The rain gave me a new antenna.
mbm-2402.quote: I was sheltering my radio gear under a fishing umbrella when I heard a distant station. The big metal ribs hadn't done the tuning, Dad said, but I still take that umbrella on clear days.

mbm-2403.clue: My crochet basket holds a bluebird's nest.
mbm-2403.quote: I crocheted a soft toy bird for my sister. The tiny nest I made came out bigger than the bird, so she keeps the bird in the nest and the nest full of spare front-door keys.

mbm-2404.clue: My helmet had an applause button.
mbm-2404.quote: On our first river trip my friend tapped my helmet every time we finished a rapid. At the quiet stretch I reached across with my paddle laid down and tapped hers. We both took a bow.

mbm-2405.clue: The club raffle has one very hard question.
mbm-2405.quote: We watch an animation with the sound off and try to draw the noise. My friend drew a school bell as three round lemons. I can hear it every time I look at the picture.

mbm-2406.clue: My chalk print has a little extra finger.
mbm-2406.quote: After lifting I slapped my chalky hand on the blackboard beside my new number. My daughter pressed her tiny hand right inside it. That's the mark I want to beat the least.

mbm-2407.clue: I can hear the bandstand in the blue patch.
mbm-2407.quote: A thunderstorm ended our town concert halfway through a polka. I saved the wet gingham from our picnic basket and used it in a quilt. I whistle the missing half when I tuck it in.

mbm-2408.clue: I know a great ending by the bus stop.
mbm-2408.quote: My pocket book fell apart and the last page stuck to my coat in the rain. I flattened it under glass. That last line lives by the front door now.

mbm-2409.clue: I give my queen the sunny side.
mbm-2409.quote: My park opponent’s glasses catch the glare in late afternoon. We turn the whole board a quarter turn and move our chairs. People think we invented sideways chess.

mbm-2410.clue: My favorite lens cap is cardboard.
mbm-2410.quote: I lost the original on a ferry. My cousin drew an eye on a circle cut from a biscuit box. Now my camera looks awake even when it's asleep.

mbm-2411.clue: I owe my best rhythm to the broom.
mbm-2411.quote: Mum swept the porch in time when we practiced son. I learned to hear the offbeat in that soft scrape. She comes to our sessions and I make sure her chair is near enough to hear my claves.

mbm-2412.clue: I have a private finish line under a bridge.
mbm-2412.quote: A chalk snail appeared on a wall beside my running route. I tap the wall each time I pass it. On my slow days I'm still faster than the snail.

mbm-2413.clue: The ski rope picked up my brother's laugh.
mbm-2413.quote: I wore a waterproof camera on the boat to film my first run on one ski. The picture was mostly my elbow. I kept the tape for the sound of my brother laughing when I waved.

mbm-2414.quote: I crocheted six red berries for a friend's play kitchen. One came out enormous. Her son promoted that one to birthday cake and stuck a wooden candle in it.

mbm-2415.clue: My notebook has a seat on the train.
mbm-2415.quote: I write one sentence for every station we pass. When the train stopped between stations I had to leave my detective balanced on a drainpipe for twenty minutes.

mbm-2416.clue: My leather strap fits a tin trumpet.
mbm-2416.quote: I made my cousin a strap for the battered little trumpet he carried to practice. I stamped stars underneath. He can feel them through his fingers before the first note.

mbm-2417.clue: A double feature takes one bag of buttons.
mbm-2417.quote: I take a button for every character I think will solve the mystery. My friend watches me shifting them from pocket to pocket. She once guessed the culprit just by the racket I made.

mbm-2418.clue: The pocketknife case has a thumbprint.
mbm-2418.quote: I pressed the leather while it was still damp and left a thumbprint beside the snap. Dad carries it on his belt. He says he can shake my hand without putting down his fishing rod.

mbm-2419.clue: I count the floorboards before a bow.
mbm-2419.quote: Our old training hall had a board that squeaked under my left foot. When I returned as a teacher it still squeaked on cue. I had trouble keeping a straight face at my first bow.

mbm-2420.clue: The sand keeps one page for itself.
mbm-2420.quote: I fell asleep reading on my towel and a breeze outlined my bookmark in sand. I drew the shape on the next page so I'd remember the chapter where the beach took over.

mbm-2421.clue: A teacup can pay the bus fare.
mbm-2421.quote: At the flea market I found a saucer to match a seller's lonely cup two stalls down. I carried them together. The smile on her face was worth my walk home.

mbm-2422.clue: My first board has a trapdoor.
mbm-2422.quote: I built our game board on a shoebox lid and one square tore loose. Now anyone landing there has to fish their pawn out of the dungeon. My friends aim for it.

mbm-2423.clue: I hang my tools by their shadows.
mbm-2423.quote: I cut scraps of dark leather the shape of each punch and hung them behind my rack. If a shadow shows after work, I know which tool is hiding in the shavings.

mbm-2424.clue: The rock shaped like a potato knows my name.
mbm-2424.quote: Our raft guide asked us to greet each landmark. I yelled hello to a potato-shaped boulder and heard a kid on the bank yell it back. We waved until the bend hid us.

mbm-2425.clue: My beach chair has a library card.
mbm-2425.quote: I glued a cloth pocket to the back of my lounger and pass it round full of paperbacks. Friends leave a ticket stub in the pocket for each book they finish in the sun.
